Author: Anand Pathak

 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh

 (Mahesh Ahuja Vs The State Of Madhya Prades
 Dated : 04-05-2023

entities.text:
High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 At Gwalior
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Shri Pawan Dwivedi, learned counsel for the petitioner.

Shri Anil Shukla, learned Public Prosecutor for the resp Heard on I.A. No. 7873/2023, which is an application under Section 397(1) of the Cr.P.C. for suspension of jail sentence of the petitioner herein.

The present revision has been preferred on behalf of the petitioner against the judgement dated 26.04.2023 passed in CRA No. 256/2022 by learned 9th Additional Sessions Judge, Gwalior whereby affirming the judgement of conviction and punishment dated 11.05.2023 in Criminal Case No. 7471/2011 passed by Special Judge, under Prevention of Food Adulteration Act/JMFC, Gwalior.

entities.text: Prevention of Food Adulteration Act/JMFC, Gwalior
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The petitioner has been convicted under Sections 7 (i), r/w 16 (1) (a) (i) and 7 (ii) r/w 16 (1) (a) (i) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 and under Section 7 (v) r/w rule 44J & 16 (1) (a) (i) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 and Prevention of Food Adulteration Rule, 1955 and sentenced to undergo RI for 6-6 months with fine of Rs.2000-2000/-, with default stipulations.

It is the submission of the learned counsel for the petitioner that he is the owner of a general store and he has no role to play regarding packaging and mixture of tobacco items as alleged against him.

Trial Court ignored the relevant provisions of Cigarettes and Other Tobacco Products (Prohibition of Advertisement and Regulation of Trade and Commerce, Production, Supply and Distribution) Act,
2003.

entities.text:
Cigarettes and Other Tobacco Products (Prohibition of Advertisement and Regulation of Trade and Commerce, Production, Supply and Distribution) Act,
2003
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: This Act does not entitle the authorities to proceed against the petitioner.

He is ready to advance arguments finally and does not intend to delay the matter, however, he seeks suspension of sentence of the petitioner as he has already suffered almost 10 days' incarceration and the total sentence awarded is of six months.
He further submits that the fine amount has already been deposited.
Considering the submissions and the facts and circumstances, this Court intends to allow the application temporarily for the time being so that the matter can be heard finally.
The petitioner shall be released on bail upon furnishing bail bond of Rs. 50,000/- (Rs. Fifty Thousand only) with one solvent surety a to the satisfaction of Trial Court.
